external_research.principle: Native and custom buttons support activation with both Space and Enter.
external_research.application: The viewport Space handler should yield when a button or its descendant owns the event.
external_research.product_fit_rationale: Both editors contain native buttons and custom menu/tab actions; preserving established activation removes a shortcut collision without changing focus order.

external_research.principle: Functionality should remain keyboard operable without requiring specific timings for individual keystrokes.
external_research.application: The guidance provides context for treating global keyboard interception cautiously; because Enter remained available, it does not by itself prove this product failed the success criterion.
external_research.product_fit_rationale: The bounded correction improves conventional keyboard operation while preserving Space-based viewport panning.

findings.surface: Shared PreviewViewport in Disc and Case Insert
findings.workflow: Activate a focused control with Space or use Space plus primary drag to pan
findings.current_behavior: Audit baseline: a window keydown handler prevented Space outside a narrow form-target list and armed pan; native/custom controls and effective contenteditable variants were not fully recognized, armed primary-pointer pan could start from an interactive target, and window blur could leave Space pan armed.
findings.local_prototype_behavior: The viewport yields Space to native/custom interactive targets and previously prevented events, rejects interactive armed-primary starts, disarms through one Space-key-up/window-blur callback, and clears the armed ref during listener cleanup without scheduling an unmount state update.
findings.user_problem: Space can fail to activate a focused control and can convert a control interaction into viewport panning.
evidence: src/components/preview/PreviewViewport.tsx window keyboard and pointer capture paths
Both Disc and Case Insert mount the shared viewport
affected_user_type: Power users who pan with Space
findings.proposed_outcome: Interactive controls retain Space activation while noninteractive preview context retains Space plus primary-drag pan; middle-button pan remains unchanged.
findings.possible_solution: Use a viewport-local input policy that respects defaultPrevented/repeat, browser-effective contenteditable, native interactive descendants, roles button/tab/menuitem, interactive pointer targets, and shared key-up/blur disarming with unmount-safe cleanup. This was prototyped locally but is not included or accepted by this publication.
tests: Source-wiring contract for shared key-up/blur disarming and unmount-safe cleanup
Native control activation and pan smoke in both editors
findings.native_verification: Required at 900×650, 1000×720, and 1920×1009 for actual platform default activation; no native verification performed in this audit.
findings.audit_time_decision: Selected as the first coherent improvement.
findings.implementation_status: local prototype exists; not published or accepted; native validation pending
findings.classification_note: The external guidance supports expected Space and Enter activation for buttons. Linked anchors are also yielded to so browser/application behavior is not overridden, not because links normally activate with Space. Because Enter remained available, this is classified as a platform-convention/accessibility best-practice break, not automatically a WCAG failure.

findings.surface: Home and both editors' project lifecycle actions
findings.workflow: New Disc, New Case Insert, Load, and cross-editor replacement
findings.current_behavior: Audit baseline: Disc New asked before reset, while Case New and Load did not consistently guard replacement; Disc-to-Case and Main Menu copy promised in-memory retention despite reset behavior and no Resume path.
findings.local_prototype_behavior: appProjectTransitions derives one policy from activeWorkspace and intent only. Initial Home New Disc/New Case/Load bypass confirmation. Active Disc/Case Main Menu closes through one truthful warning; same-type New, cross-type New, and valid Load replace through one truthful warning naming the active project. Decline invokes no reset, cleanup, apply, or workspace callback; accepted transitions reuse existing owners. Load prepares a valid restored candidate before the gate and applies it only after acceptance. A stable coordinator acquires admission synchronously at each outer New Disc, New Case Insert, Load, and Main Menu handler. While one is pending, later lifecycle attempts are rejected rather than queued and run no dialog/read/reset/apply/workspace work; normal status announces `Another project action is still in progress. Wait for it to finish, then try again.` and Home mirrors it visibly while active. Admission releases after resolution, decline, or rejection so retry works. Picker cancellation, invalid contents, restore failure, and declined replacement never apply state; decline reports `Load cancelled. Current project was kept.` Existing #300 Home feedback routing remains. No dirty/session marker, Resume promise, disabled control, or progress UI was added.
findings.user_problem: Users can lose unsaved work and cannot predict which lifecycle actions are destructive.
evidence: src/app/appProjectTransitions.ts active-workspace/intent prompt policy and synchronous single-flight coordinator
src/app/App.tsx exactly-once public New/Load/Main Menu admission and existing transition callbacks
src/app/appProjectTransitions.test.ts Home/editor matrix, deferred admission/retry/rejection, busy feedback, and App wiring
src/app/appProjectLoad.test.ts accepted/declined order, early exits, no-setter decline, deferred Load race, and #300 outcomes
findings.proposed_outcome: All destructive replacements share one truthful, cancellation-safe policy.
findings.possible_solution: Centralize the active-workspace/intent warning matrix and synchronous single-flight admission, reuse existing reset/cleanup callbacks after acceptance, and use a two-phase Load whose restored candidate reaches the existing apply owner only after acceptance. This was prototyped locally but is not included or accepted by this publication; it adds no dirty/session/Resume system, queue, generation token, cancellation mechanism, disabled control, or progress UI.
findings.architectural_owner: App project transition policy, single-flight lifecycle admission, and two-phase load orchestration
tests: Disc/Case close, same-type New, cross-type New, and Load matrix
Exact copy/options and accept/decline exactly-once operations
Stable coordinator and exactly-once entry by all four public handlers
Deferred first action rejects concurrent work and permits retry after resolution/rejection
Home busy feedback uses normal and visible Home status
Deferred Load rejects New/Main Menu/second Load without a second picker, reset, apply, or workspace mutation
Both Load routes prepare candidate before gate and apply only after acceptance

findings.audit_time_decision: Selected as the iteration-6 improvement after issue/design review.

App captures Home origin, mirrors non-success feedback only for that origin, clears stale Home feedback after success, and preserves the existing editor announcement path. The existing Home message has role=status.

findings.surface: Disc and Case Insert PNG export
findings.workflow: Export a design with preflight warnings or blockers
findings.current_behavior: Audit baseline: the save destination dialog opened before preflight, and tests locked that order.
findings.local_prototype_behavior: Both routes build and confirm their existing preflight before Save. Rejection skips Save/render/write with the existing preflight-cancel status; post-approval Save cancellation skips render/write with the existing export-cancel status. Successful paths preserve filename defaults, DPI, preflight content/options, renderer arguments, guides, write commands, and messages. Disc preview measurement remains deferred until rendering after destination selection.
findings.user_problem: Users choose a path before learning that export needs review, causing needless native-dialog churn.
evidence: src/app/appPngExport.ts preflight-first orchestration for both routes
src/app/appPngExport.test.ts rejection, Save-cancellation, successful-order, preserved-input/default, and deferred-measurement contracts
affected_user_type: All users exporting incomplete or warning-bearing designs
findings.possible_solution: Reorder only the established orchestration to build preflight → confirm → Save destination → render → write while preserving current route inputs, outputs, and messages. This was prototyped locally but is not included or accepted by this publication.
tests: Both routes stop after a cancelled post-approval Save
Successful case and disc order is preflight → confirm → Save → render → write
Case pane/disc defaults and renderer inputs remain stable
Disc preview measurement occurs only when rendering proceeds

findings.workflow: Enter an invalid or inconsistent dimension
findings.current_behavior: Normalization preserves the old controlled value; the field snaps back without an explanation.
findings.user_problem: Users cannot tell why input was rejected or how to correct it.
findings.frequency: Low-to-medium overall; high within custom-template use
findings.proposed_outcome: Invalid values have specific, accessible, correctable guidance.
findings.possible_solution: Return structured domain validation and render associated field errors while committing only valid normalized values.
findings.native_verification: Required for focus, error visibility, and narrow layouts.

findings.workflow: Submit overlapping Steam searches and choose a result
findings.current_behavior: Audit baseline: searches had no latest-submission ownership, so an older completion could overwrite newer results, announce a stale failure, or clear loading while a newer Enter-submitted search remained pending. Reset and Clear could also be undone by an older completion.
findings.local_prototype_behavior: useSteamImport owns one stable monotonically increasing submission coordinator. Every submitted query supersedes older work, and only the newest submission may publish results, announce success/no-results/failure, or clear search loading. A submitted empty query invalidates pending work, clears loading, and retains `Enter a Steam game title or App ID to search.` Existing resetSteamImportState and clearSteamSearchResults also invalidate pending work and clear loading, so stale completions cannot repopulate cleared state. Requests finish normally; no AbortController, debounce, cache, pagination, Enter disabling, Steam-import concurrency change, or result-UI change was added.
findings.user_problem: Users can select a result from the wrong query.
evidence: src/hooks/useSteamImport.ts stable coordinator instance and reset/clear integration
src/hooks/steamSearchSubmission.ts monotonic identity and latest-only publication
src/hooks/steamSearchSubmission.test.ts deferred ordering, stale failure, pending loading, invalidation, current outcomes, and hook wiring
src/components/sidebar/GamePanel.tsx preserved overlapping Enter path and result presentation
affected_user_type: Steam import users on slow or variable connections
findings.proposed_outcome: Only the newest submitted query may publish results or terminal feedback and clear loading; explicit invalidation prevents stale repopulation.
findings.possible_solution: Give the Steam-search hook a stable monotonic submission coordinator, gate every completion effect on latest identity, and invalidate through existing empty/reset/clear owners. This was prototyped locally but is not included or accepted by this publication.
findings.architectural_owner: Steam-search submission state adjacent to the existing Steam import hook

findings.workflow: Determine and switch the active ribbon category
findings.current_behavior: Audit baseline: active category was represented by an is-active CSS class without equivalent selected/pressed/tab semantics.
findings.local_prototype_behavior: Each existing native category button binds aria-pressed directly to activeTab === tab.id; the container is a named group. Labels, order, focus/click behavior, and layout are unchanged.
findings.user_problem: Assistive technology cannot reliably identify the current category.
findings.proposed_outcome: Assistive technology can identify the active category while existing native-button interaction remains unchanged.
findings.possible_solution: Bind aria-pressed on the existing mapped native buttons to authoritative activeTab equality and name their exclusive category group. This was prototyped locally but is not included or accepted by this publication; no tablist or keyboard model was added.
findings.architectural_owner: Inline preview text editor ribbon category semantics
tests: Source contract that the mapped native button template binds aria-pressed to activeTab === tab.id

findings.surface: Home and Case Insert capability/status copy
findings.workflow: Choose Load, New Disc, or New Case Insert at launch
findings.current_behavior: Home says only Disc projects load and Case Insert is future work, while Case projects route and the Case editor is active but incomplete.
findings.user_problem: Users receive conflicting product capability expectations.
findings.proposed_outcome: One truthful vocabulary distinguishes active, alpha, and incomplete features.
findings.possible_solution: Centralize capability labels/status and consume them on Home and editor entry points.
findings.native_verification: Not required unless revised copy changes layout.

findings.workflow: Save repeatedly, return to Main Menu, resume, and understand dirty state
findings.current_behavior: Save always behaves as Save As; there is no current path, dirty flag, or resume affordance; transient status also carries file status.
findings.user_problem: Users cannot tell whether work is saved or resume the in-memory work promised by transition copy.
findings.proposed_outcome: Explicit current project identity, dirty state, Save/Save As, and truthful resume/replacement lifecycle.
findings.possible_solution: Design a focused project-session domain before changing UI; route transitions/persistence through it.
findings.confidence_note: The gap is directly evidenced; the solution remains broad and requires design.

findings.workflow: Open, navigate, choose, and dismiss with keyboard/assistive technology
findings.current_behavior: The aria-modal dialog does not establish initial focus, contain focus, or restore focus to its trigger.
findings.user_problem: Focus can remain behind the modal or become lost after close.
findings.proposed_outcome: Focus enters, stays within, and returns from the modal predictably.
findings.possible_solution: Add a picker-scoped focus lifecycle keyed to open/close and trigger identity.
findings.confidence_note: Static lifecycle evidence is direct; runtime focus behavior still needs confirmation.

findings.workflow: Import a Steam game into a fresh/default Case project
findings.current_behavior: Import populates back-cover text while visibility stays disabled, then reports success without noting that the content is hidden.
findings.user_problem: Users may think import failed or hunt for the enable control.
affected_user_type: Case Insert users relying on Steam metadata
findings.proposed_outcome: Feedback accurately states hidden imported content, or import deliberately enables it under a documented rule.
findings.possible_solution: Prefer explicit follow-up feedback unless product decides import should enable while preserving prior user intent.
findings.confidence_note: State/result evidence is direct; auto-enable versus explanatory feedback remains a product decision.

findings.surface: Disc template transitions and positioned content
findings.current_behavior: Template changes immediately clamp multiple owners; returning does not restore prior layout and there is no warning/undo.
findings.user_problem: Exploratory template comparison can silently damage a carefully positioned design.
findings.proposed_outcome: Template-induced changes are understood and recoverable.
findings.possible_solution: Evaluate pre-change warning plus one-step restore or template-keyed snapshots before changing domain state.
findings.architectural_owner: Disc template transition domain and placement owners
findings.confidence_note: Clamping is directly evidenced; the recovery model still needs design.

findings.workflow: Save during interruption, disk-full, or process failure
findings.current_behavior: The Rust command directly overwrites the destination via std::fs::write.
findings.user_problem: A rare interrupted save can destroy the last usable project copy.
findings.proposed_outcome: A failed save leaves the prior file intact and reports failure.
findings.possible_solution: Write/sync a sibling temporary file and replace atomically with platform-aware cleanup/error handling.

findings.surface: Case Insert Back and Spine role navigation
findings.workflow: Open Back Additional Artwork or Spine duplicate Steam Branding
findings.current_behavior: Audit baseline: visible roles had no owner and rendered issue-placeholder copy; Spine duplicated a Steam Branding concept already owned by its setup panel.
findings.local_prototype_behavior: Back no longer inventories unsupported Additional Artwork, Spine no longer inventories Steam Branding as a role, and the unused steam-backup-branding role ID type member is removed after a repository-wide owner search found no runtime consumer. Dedicated Spine Steam Branding and Front/Spine Additional Artwork controls remain wired. The generic ticket fallback is unchanged, and an invariant proves no current Case role inventory can reach it.
findings.user_problem: Production navigation leads to dead ends and exposes internal issue language.
evidence: src/editor/editorNavigationShell.ts corrected Back and Spine inventories and role ID union
src/components/caseInsert/CaseInsertEditorShell.test.ts setup-panel, Additional Artwork, and owner-invariant contracts
findings.proposed_outcome: Every visible role opens real controls; unavailable roles stay absent.
findings.possible_solution: Remove only the two invalid inventory entries, remove the newly unused role ID type member, and enforce that every visible Case role maps to an existing owner while retaining the generic fallback and real setup/role panels. This was prototyped locally but is not included or accepted by this publication.

tests: Spine omits the Steam Branding role while its dedicated setup panel remains wired

findings.workflow: Choose a candidate whose apply step fails but resolves
findings.current_behavior: The picker closes after any fulfilled onSelect, while some callers swallow failures and resolve.
findings.user_problem: The picker disappears on failure and loses retry context.
findings.proposed_outcome: The picker closes only after confirmed successful application.
findings.possible_solution: Use an explicit success result or require rejected failure, then centralize close/error behavior.
